tasks.gr10-electrostatics-electric-circuits-t1: Grade 10 Physical Sciences Term 1: Electrostatics — Coulomb's law, electric fields; introductory electric circuits — Ohm's law.
tasks.gr10-waves-sound-light-t1: Grade 10 Physical Sciences Term 1: Transverse and longitudinal waves, properties of sound and light.
tasks.gr10-pulses-superposition-t1: Topic: Transverse pulses and superposition. Cover a pulse, a transverse pulse (particles move at right angles to the direction of travel), amplitude as the maximum disturbance from the rest position, pulse speed = distance / time, superposition as the addition of disturbances of pulses in the same place at the same time, constructive and destructive interference with signed amplitudes, and that pulses pass through each other unchanged. Ask Grade 10 learners to add amplitudes with signs and to calculate pulse speed and distance.
tasks.gr10-em-radiation-t1: Topic: Electromagnetic radiation. Cover the source (an accelerating charge), oscillating electric and magnetic fields at right angles, no medium needed, c = 3,00 × 10⁸ m·s⁻¹ in a vacuum, the wave-particle duality, the order of the EM spectrum by frequency and wavelength, c = fλ, photon energy E = hf = hc/λ with h = 6,63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, a use of each type, penetrating ability, the dangers of gamma rays, X-rays and ultraviolet, and cellphone radiation. State c and h in every question that needs them. Ask Grade 10 learners to order the spectrum and to calculate frequency, wavelength and photon energy.
tasks.gr10-matter-classification-t1: Topic: Revision of matter and classification. Cover elements, compounds, pure substances and homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures, formulae of ionic compounds from the charges of the ions (NaCl, MgO, CaCl2, Al2O3) and names ending in -ide, metals and non-metals, electrical and thermal conductors and insulators, and magnetic materials (iron, cobalt and nickel). Ask Grade 10 learners to classify matter and to write ionic formulae from stated ion charges.
tasks.gr10-atom-isotopes-t1: Topic: The atom and isotopes. Cover the development of models of the atom (Dalton, Thomson, Rutherford with the gold foil evidence for a nucleus, Bohr energy levels), atomic number Z as the number of protons, mass number A as protons plus neutrons, neutrons = A − Z, electrons in neutral atoms and ions, isotopes as atoms with the same Z but different A, and relative atomic mass as the average of isotope masses weighted by abundance (chlorine 75% Cl-35 and 25% Cl-37 gives 35,5). Ask Grade 10 learners to count particles and to calculate relative atomic mass to one decimal place.
tasks.gr10-longitudinal-waves-t1: Topic: Longitudinal waves. Cover a longitudinal wave on a spring (particles move parallel to the direction of travel), compressions and rarefactions, wavelength as the distance between two successive compressions, frequency in hertz, period T = 1/f, wave speed v = fλ, and the comparison with transverse waves (crests and troughs). Ask Grade 10 learners to calculate wavelength, frequency, period and speed.
tasks.gr10-sound-t1: Topic: Sound. Cover sound as a longitudinal wave that needs a medium, its speed in solids, liquids and gases (use 340 m·s⁻¹ in air and quote it in the question), pitch and frequency, loudness and amplitude, tone, the audible range of about 20 Hz to 20 000 Hz, infrasound and ultrasound with uses, and echoes (distance = speed × time ÷ 2). Ask Grade 10 learners to calculate wavelength, travel time and echo distance.
